6-hydroxynorsalvinorin metabolite — could not confirm primary literature; salvinorin B is the dominant documented metabolite
notes: The only non-nitrogenous opioid agonist known. Smoked: onset <30 s, peak 1–2 min, gone by 15–20 min. Brain Cmax 40 s after IV in baboons, brain t½ ~8 min — explains the short duration despite ~75-min plasma half-life in rodents. Sublingual/buccal needs vehicle (DMSO/PEG); oral inactive (esterase hydrolysis). Phenomenology is mechanistically third-kind: no 5-HT2A, no NMDA — pure KOR agonism with β-arrestin-driven dissociation/dysphoria.

name: Salvinorin B

binding.assay_buffer_notes: Multiple reports place Sal B Ki >1000 nM (≈250-fold weaker than Sal A); some report values in the 65–418 nM range cited for divinatorin D/E and Sal B together (reviews). Generally considered the inactive plasma metabolite of Sal A.
binding.notes: Loss of the C-2 acetoxy → essentially loss of KOR affinity. Sal B is the principal C-2-deacetyl metabolite of Sal A produced by plasma carboxylesterase, and is behaviourally inactive in animals.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Negligible KOR engagement — its biological role is as the inactive principal metabolite of salvinorin A and as a synthetic precursor to the C-2 ether analogues (MOM-Sal B, EOM-Sal B, mesyl Sal B).

data_gaps_remaining: Precise Ki value at human KOR — most papers simply report >1 µM
notes: C-2 hydroxyl (rather than acetoxy) — confirms the C-2 acyl group as critical for KOR pharmacophore. Useful only as a synthetic scaffold for C-2 modified analogues.

name: Salvinorin B ethoxymethyl ether

binding.assay_buffer_notes: Ki = 3.1 ± 0.4 nM (Sal A in same assay: 7.4 ± 0.7 nM; β-THP-Sal B: 6.2 ± 0.4 nM).
binding.notes: C-2 ethoxymethyl ether — replaces metabolically labile acetate, gives both higher affinity and dramatically extended duration.

biased_agonism.interpretation: G-protein-biased in cellular assays. Substitution of C-2 ethoxymethyl ether for the C-2 acetyl group of Sal A reduces JNK stimulation, prevents desensitisation, and gives a monotonic antinociceptive dose-response. Associated with anti-cocaine efficacy with fewer KOR side effects (less anxiogenic/anhedonic).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: KOR Gαi/o (cAMP↓, GIRK↑) with reduced β-arrestin-2 recruitment and reduced JNK activation. In MS preclinical models (EAE) shows KOR-dependent disease modification — possibly via myelin-OL-progenitor effects.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Reduced acute desensitisation vs Sal A (Bruchas group — C-2 ether prevents the rapid JNK-mediated KOR desensitisation seen with Sal A).

notes: C-2 ethoxymethyl ether of Sal B — the SAR archetype for trading metabolic lability for longer duration. Increased KOR affinity AND functionally G-protein-biased; among the more interesting therapeutic-candidate Sal analogues, with preclinical activity in cocaine seeking and EAE/MS remyelination.

name: Salvinorin C

binding.assay_buffer_notes: Ki = 1022 ± 262 nM — ~250-fold weaker than Sal A
binding.notes: Béguin et al. 2005 — Sal C natural extra acetoxy at C-1 (1α-acetoxy) reduces affinity significantly, supporting the Sal A pharmacophore hypothesis that C-1 substitution disfavours KOR binding.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Minimal in vivo activity reported.

notes: Natural minor constituent of S. divinorum. ~250× weaker at KOR than Sal A. No reported human psychoactivity.

name: Scopolamine

binding.tissue_or_cell: CHO-K1 cells expressing cloned human M1
binding.assay_buffer_notes: Standard membrane binding, 25°C; values from Buckley et al. 1989 (CHO-K1 cloned receptors) and PDSP compilations.
binding.reference: pmid:2704370 (Buckley NJ et al. — Antagonist binding properties of five cloned muscarinic receptors expressed in CHO-K1 cells; Mol Pharmacol 1989)
binding.notes: Scopolamine is broadly equipotent across M1-M5 in cloned binding assays, with Ki values typically <1 nM at all five subtypes. The 'non-selective' description is accurate at the equilibrium binding level — apparent functional selectivity in vivo arises from differential CNS penetration vs peripheral exposure and from kinetic differences (slower off-rate at some subtypes).

binding.tissue_or_cell: CHO-K1 cells expressing cloned human M2
CHO-K1 cells expressing cloned human M3
CHO-K1 cells expressing cloned human M4
CHO-K1 cells expressing cloned human M5
HEK293 stably expressing human 5-HT3A; whole-cell patch clamp
binding.reference: pmid:27077139 (Lummis SCR group — The muscarinic antagonists scopolamine and atropine are competitive antagonists at 5-HT3 receptors; doi:10.1111/jnc.13628)
binding.notes: Competitive 5-HT3 antagonism (IC50 ~2 µM) — likely contributes to scopolamine's modest antiemetic action independent of muscarinic block, particularly in motion sickness.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Pan-muscarinic antagonism: blocks Gαq/PLCβ at M1/M3/M5 (postsynaptic, predominantly cortical/hippocampal/glandular) and Gαi/AC inhibition at M2/M4 (presynaptic autoreceptors). In the PFC, M1 antagonism on GABAergic interneurons appears responsible for the rapid disinhibition-driven glutamate surge underlying scopolamine's rapid antidepressant effect (Voleti et al. 2013; Witkin et al. 2014). The same M1 antagonism in cortex/hippocampus drives the well-known memory impairment and delirium at higher doses.

neuroimaging.finding: Scopolamine produces characteristic increase in delta and theta power and decrease in alpha/beta — the 'cholinergic deficit EEG' signature also seen in Alzheimer's disease, supporting its use as a pharmacological model of AD cognitive impairment.
neuroimaging.reference: doi:10.1111/j.1365-2125.2011.03936.x (Liem-Moolenaar M et al. — PK-PD relationships of CNS effects of scopolamine in healthy subjects; Br J Clin Pharmacol 2011)

neuroimaging.finding: 0.4 mg scopolamine reduces task-related activation in hippocampus, parahippocampal cortex, and medial prefrontal cortex during memory encoding; effect reversible with donepezil.

routes.reference: doi:10.1023/A:1015916423156 (Putcha L et al. — Pharmacokinetics and oral bioavailability of scopolamine in normal subjects; Pharm Res 1989)
routes.notes: Bioavailability ranged 10.7-48.2% — highly variable. Cmax 528.6 ± 109.4 pg/mL. Oral PO is unreliable; transdermal or parenteral routes preferred for clinical use.

routes.reference: pmid:16175141 (Renner UD, Oertel R, Kirch W — Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in clinical use of scopolamine; Ther Drug Monit 2005)
routes.notes: Mean Cmax 2909.8 ± 240.9 pg/mL after 0.4 mg IV; mean terminal t1/2 ~1.5 h IV (range 1.2-2.5 h). Plasma declines biexponentially with rapid distribution phase.

1.5 mg Transderm Scōp patch delivers ~0.5 mg over 72 h; steady-state plasma 56-245 pg/mL maintained over 72 h. Protective effect emerges 6-8 h after application; clinically used for motion sickness and post-operative nausea.

routes.reference: pmid:25187210 (Wu et al. — Dose escalation pharmacokinetics of intranasal scopolamine gel; J Clin Pharmacol 2015)
routes.notes: Intranasal gel 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 mg showed linear PK; Tmax ~1.3 h. Higher bioavailability than oral by bypassing first-pass.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Increased oral scopolamine AUC by reducing first-pass metabolism — clinically observed.
Expected increase in scopolamine exposure; formal interaction studies sparse

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic antagonism (raise synaptic ACh to outcompete scopolamine)
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Reverses scopolamine-induced delirium, memory impairment, and tachycardia. Physostigmine is the antidote of choice for anticholinergic toxidrome.
drug_interactions_pk.reference: pmid:25339374 (Physostigmine is the antidote for anticholinergic syndrome)

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP3A5*1 carriers (expressers) may have somewhat faster clearance; no formal large-cohort PK study published. CYP3A4 induction (rifampin, phenytoin) will reduce scopolamine exposure; inhibition (azoles, macrolides, grapefruit) increases it.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Chronic scopolamine in animal models produces muscarinic receptor upregulation (compensatory) within ~5-7 days. In humans, tolerance to the sedating and anti-motion-sickness effects develops over days; tolerance to memory-impairment effects is incomplete.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Discontinuation after sustained transdermal use (>72 h) can produce a rebound syndrome with dizziness, nausea, headache, sweating, abdominal cramps, and bradycardia (cholinergic rebound) lasting 1-3 days. Most pronounced when patches are abruptly stopped after multi-week scuba-diving or post-surgical use.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Scopolamine is not a clinically significant hERG blocker at therapeutic concentrations. Tachycardia and modest QT changes in overdose are predominantly mediated by vagal withdrawal (M2 blockade on SA node) rather than direct ion channel block.
Weak nAChR antagonism at high concentrations (µM range); not clinically relevant at therapeutic doses.

demographic_differences.sex: Women have somewhat greater sensitivity to CNS effects (memory, sedation) at equivalent plasma concentrations; mechanism unclear, possibly progesterone modulation of muscarinic signaling. No major PK sex difference.
demographic_differences.age: Elderly are markedly more sensitive to delirium-inducing effects (Beers criteria — avoid). Pediatric patients show paradoxical excitement and severe anticholinergic toxicity at lower doses; transdermal scopolamine is contraindicated in children <12.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal impairment has minor effect (only 2.6% excreted unchanged); hepatic impairment (CYP3A4) substantially prolongs clearance.

data_gaps_remaining: Specific PDSP Ki values for scopolamine at human M1-M5 — primary Buckley 1989 paper not directly accessed (PDSP compilation values used)
No published hERG IC50 for scopolamine
notes: Scopolamine is the prototypical CNS-penetrant tropane alkaloid muscarinic antagonist — the high BBB permeability of the parent compound (vs the quaternary peripheral analogues N-butylscopolamine/hyoscine butylbromide and glycopyrrolate) is what distinguishes it. Acts as a non-selective M1-M5 antagonist in binding assays (~0.4-0.6 nM at all subtypes), but its clinical CNS-selectivity profile vs atropine is mostly explained by its higher CNS:peripheral concentration ratio (3-4× atropine's) and greater oral CNS-side-effect profile. The rapid antidepressant action (Drevets / Furey trials, 4 µg/kg IV) appears M1-mediated via PFC GABAergic interneuron disinhibition → glutamate surge → BDNF → mTORC1 — similar final pathway to ketamine. The deliriant profile at recreational doses (oral 1-4 mg, or seeds of Datura/Brugmansia) reflects pan-cortical M1 antagonism producing true (non-insight) hallucinations and amnesia. Datura/Brugmansia content is unpredictable: scopolamine/hyoscyamine/atropine ratios vary 10-40× between specimens, seasons, soils, and plant parts, making botanical preparations exceptionally dangerous.

name: Semax

primary_targets: BDNF/NGF upregulation in hippocampus and cortex

functional.notes: Single intranasal semax dose increases BDNF mRNA ~3× in hippocampus and TrkB phosphorylation ~1.6× within hours; effect peaks 8 h, sustained 12-24 h via active metabolite Pro-Gly-Pro.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Semax is rapidly cleaved (plasma t½ 2-5 min) but the active metabolite Pro-Gly-Pro (PGP) accumulates in brain and acts as a weak enkephalinase inhibitor, prolonging endogenous enkephalin signaling and BDNF transcription. routes.notes: Parent peptide t½ 2-5 min in plasma; intranasal route bypasses GI proteolysis. BBB penetrance via olfactory/trigeminal pathway; hippocampal/cortical accumulation within 30-60 min.

metabolism.notes: PGP is itself biologically active, brain-accumulating, and responsible for the prolonged BDNF/NGF mRNA upregulation.

data_gaps_remaining: independent Western validation of clinical claims
notes: Synthetic analog of ACTH(4-10) with the N-terminal phenylalanine replaced and a C-terminal Pro-Gly-Pro tail for metabolic stabilization. Approved in Russia for stroke and cognitive disorders. name: Sulbutiamine

primary_targets: dopamine D1 receptor density (chronic upregulation in PFC)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Lipophilic thiamine prodrug — two thiamine molecules linked by a disulfide bridge, esterified with isobutyrate. Crosses BBB more efficiently than thiamine hydrochloride. After reduction to thiamine in CNS, supports TPP-dependent metabolism (pyruvate dehydrogenase, α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, transketolase). Chronic dosing upregulates dopamine D1 receptor density in PFC in rats.

routes.notes: Approximate t½ ~5 h; rapidly reduced/hydrolyzed to thiamine. Often dosed 200-600 mg BID.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Tolerance to mood/energy effects develops over weeks; some users report dependence-like patterns and dysphoric withdrawal — atypical for a 'vitamin'.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Anecdotal reports of depressive rebound on cessation after chronic use

notes: Approved in France as Arcalion for asthenia. Functionally a thiamine donor with central effects beyond what thiamine supplementation produces. Reported habit-forming potential in nootropic forums is consistent with chronic dopaminergic adaptation.

name: Sulforaphane

functional.readout: Nrf2 nuclear translocation, ARE-driven gene expression (NQO1, HO-1, GCL)
functional.notes: Direct covalent modification of Keap1 cysteine 151 releases Nrf2 — most potent natural-product Nrf2 activator.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Master mechanism: Keap1 thiol modification → Nrf2 stabilization → ARE-driven phase II detoxification (NQO1, GST, UGT, HO-1, GCL) → antioxidant + anti-inflammatory + anti-carcinogenic effects.

routes.notes: F up to 70% if administered as free SFN with active myrosinase; ~10% if administered as glucoraphanin precursor without myrosinase. Eliminated as thiol conjugates (mercapturic acid) in urine.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: GST null genotypes have altered SFN excretion kinetics; potentially altered efficacy in chemoprevention studies.

notes: Broccoli sprout isothiocyanate; most potent natural-product Nrf2 activator. Cognitive claims are largely extrapolated from anti-oxidant/anti-inflammatory mechanism rather than direct trial data.

name: Sunifiram

functional.readout: reversal of NBQX-induced amnesia in mouse passive avoidance; reversal of kynurenate block of NMDA-mediated [3H]NA release
functional.cell_system: in vivo behavior; rat hippocampal slice
functional.notes: CRITICAL: direct interaction of sunifiram with AMPA receptors has NEVER been demonstrated in vitro. All evidence for AMPA involvement is indirect (pharmacological antagonism of the antiamnesic effect by NBQX). The Romanelli/Galeotti papers explicitly note the absence of direct binding data.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mechanism of action genuinely uncertain. Authors of the original characterization suggest indirect AMPA potentiation, possibly via glycine-site facilitation of NMDA receptors leading to AMPA insertion. No primary receptor target has ever been identified by direct binding assay.

data_gaps_remaining: Direct binding constant at any receptor
Independent replication of antiamnesic activity outside the original Italian group
notes: EXTREMELY IMPORTANT: sunifiram is popularly described as an AMPAkine, but the entire evidence base is from a handful of papers by Romanelli/Galeotti/Pellegrini-Giampietro (DM-235), all using indirect pharmacological inference. No direct AMPA receptor binding has ever been demonstrated. Vendor and grey-market literature dramatically overstates the mechanistic confidence. Treat as a poorly-characterized cognition-enhancement candidate, not as a validated AMPA PAM. The 'AMPA-PAM' tag should be removed from any consumer-facing data presentation.

name: Tapentadol

binding.notes: Tzschentke 2007 — Ki 96 nM at cloned hMOR (some sources quote 60 nM at rat MOR). ~50× weaker than morphine yet only 2-3× less analgesic in vivo due to NRI synergy.
Tapentadol has only weak SERT activity (>30× selectivity for NET vs SERT) → much lower serotonin-syndrome risk than tramadol.

functional.notes: Manandhar 2022 — tapentadol has lower intrinsic efficacy at MOR than morphine or oxycodone (partial agonist character at MOR).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi + central noradrenergic inhibition → synergistic analgesia. NET-mediated descending pain modulation contributes most of analgesia at typical doses.

metabolism.notes: Glucuronidation dominates clearance — NOT CYP-dependent; minimal DDI footprint and minimal pharmacogenetic CYP impact.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Hypertensive crisis with MAOIs (contraindicated). Serotonin syndrome risk lower than tramadol because SERT activity minimal.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Unlike tramadol/codeine, tapentadol does NOT depend on CYP2D6 bioactivation — no PM/UM dichotomy. UGT2B7 polymorphisms produce modest exposure differences.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mixed opioid + adrenergic discontinuation; generally milder than morphine.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Less seizure risk than tramadol; lacks SERT activity.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: small reduction in clearance, no dose adjustment usually needed.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic: avoid in severe impairment (>3× AUC). Renal: avoid in severe CKD.

notes: Mechanistically cleaner than tramadol: NRI dominates, SERT minimal, no CYP2D6 bioactivation. Safer pharmacogenetic and DDI profile.

name: Temazepam

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Non-selective benzodiazepine-site PAM. 3-hydroxy already present → direct glucuronidation, no CYP metabolism needed.

routes.notes: t1/2 8–15 h; intermediate hypnotic duration.

metabolism.notes: Stereoselective: UGT2B7/1A9 dominant for R-temazepam; UGT2B15/1A6 for S-temazepam.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: UGT2B15 polymorphism alters S-temazepam clearance.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: minimal CL change.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Preferred in hepatic impairment (LOT rule).

data_gaps_remaining: Subunit-specific Ki not separately characterized; assumed non-selective like other 1,4-benzos

metabolism.notes: Class-default CYP3A4 N-dealkylation pathway shared with fentanyl. Also 4-ANPP (4-anilino-N-phenethylpiperidine) from amide hydrolysis is a marker of synthesis.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Increased AUC, overdose risk.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Inferred from fentanyl-class — no analogue-specific human data.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Classical opioid; typically shorter than morphine due to higher lipophilicity.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Wooden chest syndrome — class-shared; rapid IV / smoked / IV illicit exposure.

notes: Saturated furanyl analogue. Lower potency than furanylfentanyl (no ring epoxidation pathway).

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Additive serotonergic load

name: Thiopental

routes.subject_demographics: Adults; t1/2β 11 h but clinical recovery <10 min due to peripheral redistribution.
routes.notes: Classic 'context-sensitive half-life' demonstration drug — single dose is short due to redistribution; infusions accumulate dramatically.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment prolongs offset; obese patients accumulate due to large lipid Vd.

name: Tianeptine

binding.tissue_or_cell: HEK293 cells stably expressing human MOR
binding.assay_buffer_notes: standard binding buffer; mean ± SD reported as 383 ± 183 nM
binding.notes: Gassaway et al. 2014 — the seminal MOR characterization of tianeptine. Low affinity but high efficacy at MOR.

binding.tissue_or_cell: HEK293 cells stably expressing human DOR
binding.notes: ~100× weaker than MOR; functionally irrelevant at therapeutic exposures.
Negligible binding at KOR — selectivity ratio MOR >> KOR.

functional.notes: Full agonist efficacy at MOR — equivalent maximal G-protein activation to DAMGO. EC50 194 ± 70 nM.
Species shift — mouse MOR 3× less sensitive than human.
Tianeptine inhibits forskolin-stimulated cAMP via Gαi coupling at MOR — confirms canonical opioid signaling.

biased_agonism.interpretation: Tianeptine is widely reported as a MOR full agonist with reduced β-arrestin recruitment relative to DAMGO, but quantitative bias factors are sparse in the primary literature. Behavioral tolerance/dependence develops despite the proposed bias, indicating clinically meaningful arrestin signaling remains.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Tianeptine activates canonical MOR Gαi/o coupling — inhibition of adenylyl cyclase (reduced cAMP), activation of GIRK channels, inhibition of voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels. Chronic dosing produces classical MOR tolerance with reduced analgesic and locomotor responses, mediated by receptor desensitization and downregulation in mice (Frontiers Psychiatry 2023, doi:10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1186397). Downstream BDNF/TrkB upregulation in the hippocampus appears MOR-dependent (Translational Psychiatry 2017, doi:10.1038/npp.2017.60).

neuroimaging.finding: Tianeptine induces opioid-receptor-dependent β oscillations in the rat hippocampus — naloxone-reversible.

routes.notes: High oral bioavailability (~99%, range 66-100%); rapid absorption with minimal first-pass effect. Terminal t½ 2.5 ± 1.1 h. Half-life prolongs to 4-9 h in elderly. MC5 metabolite t½ 7.2 ± 5.7 h.

metabolism.notes: Primary clearance route is mitochondrial β-oxidation of the heptanoic acid side chain — NOT CYP-mediated. This is unusual among psychotropics and minimizes CYP-mediated DDIs.
Minor pathway; reactive metabolite formation has been observed but is not a dominant clearance route.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Contraindicated — risk of hypertensive crisis and opioid potentiation

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: additive CNS depression + altered tianeptine absorption
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Reduced peak tianeptine plasma levels and enhanced sedation

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: OPRM1 A118G (N40D) carriers have altered MOR signaling and altered response to opioid agonists generally; tianeptine response data per-genotype is not established but theoretically relevant given the MOR mechanism.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Chronic tianeptine produces analgesic and locomotor tolerance in mice consistent with classical MOR downregulation/desensitization within 7-14 days of repeated dosing; cross-tolerance to morphine demonstrated.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Classical opioid withdrawal — onset 6-24 h after last dose, peak 24-72 h, lasting 5-10+ days. Symptoms: anxiety, dysphoria, sweating, GI distress, myalgia, insomnia, mydriasis, rhinorrhea, piloerection. Reported clinically indistinguishable from short-acting opioid withdrawal at supratherapeutic doses (gas-station 'Zaza' / 'Tianna' cases).

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Historical 'serotonin reuptake enhancer' (SSRE) framing is unsupported by contemporary radioligand studies; tianeptine does not meaningfully alter SERT activity in humans at therapeutic concentrations. The antidepressant effect is MOR-mediated.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: t½ extended to 4-9 h; dose reduction recommended.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal impairment prolongs elimination since tianeptine and metabolites undergo renal excretion.

data_gaps_remaining: quantitative bias factor for G-protein vs β-arrestin at MOR
human PET MOR occupancy at therapeutic dose
notes: CRITICAL SAFETY: Tianeptine is a μ-opioid receptor FULL AGONIST with sub-micromolar EC50. The historical 'SSRE' / 'atypical antidepressant' framing is medically obsolete and dangerously underplays the true pharmacology. At supratherapeutic doses (>50 mg, often 500-5000 mg in abuse), tianeptine produces classical opioid intoxication, respiratory depression, addiction, and withdrawal. Numerous US gas-station products ('Zaza', 'Tianaa', 'Neptune's Fix') have caused poison-control epidemics and FDA warnings. Treat as a short-acting MOR agonist for clinical and harm-reduction purposes.

name: Tramadol

binding.notes: Raffa 1992 — parent tramadol Ki ≈ 2.1 μM (weak); analgesia largely from M1 (O-DSMT).
(+)-tramadol enantiomer dominates SERT inhibition.
(−)-tramadol enantiomer dominates NET inhibition.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Two parallel mechanisms: (1) parent tramadol + M1 → MOR Gαi cascade; (2) parent → SERT/NET inhibition → enhanced descending inhibition. M1 (O-desmethyltramadol) is the dominant opioid effector.

metabolism.notes: M1 has ≈200× higher MOR affinity than parent; clinical analgesia largely depends on M1.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: serotonin syndrome; seizure threshold lowered

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs: poor analgesia (low M1). UMs: respiratory depression from low doses, multiple paediatric deaths; FDA contraindicates tramadol in children <12 y. CPIC 2021 guideline.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Hybrid opioid + serotonergic/noradrenergic discontinuation syndrome — opioid (sweating, GI) PLUS atypical (panic, paraesthesias, hallucinations, severe insomnia) lasting 5-15 d.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Lowers seizure threshold; risk amplified by SSRIs, bupropion, TCAs, and at supratherapeutic doses.
Minor 5-HT3 antagonism may contribute to anti-emetic / analgesic profile.

demographic_differences.age: Contraindicated <12 y; caution >65 (renal/hepatic decline).
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Reduce dose in CKD and cirrhosis.

notes: The serotonergic and seizure liability separates tramadol from classical opioids and creates DDI risks (SSRIs, MAOIs, linezolid) that don't apply to morphine.

name: Tranylcypromine

binding.notes: Irreversible covalent inhibitor — forms adduct with FAD cofactor via cyclopropyl ring opening. At low doses (20 mg/d) selective for MAO-A; at higher doses also inhibits MAO-B and gains weak DAT/NET inhibition.
Off-target epigenetic effect: lysine-specific demethylase 1 inhibition. Scaffold has been re-purposed for LSD1-inhibitor cancer drugs (e.g. iadademstat).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Irreversible MAO inhibition causes accumulation of 5-HT, NE, DA, and phenethylamines. Trace amines (β-PEA, octopamine) accumulate and act as 'false neurotransmitters' on TAAR1.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic — inability to deaminate dietary tyramine
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Hypertensive crisis. 'Cheese reaction' — defining safety issue.
Serotonin syndrome; contraindicated. 5-week washout from fluoxetine, 2 weeks from other SSRIs required.
Severe hypertension. Contraindicated.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Not strongly CYP-dependent.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: MAO enzyme resynthesis ~2 weeks — pharmacodynamic effect outlasts plasma clearance by weeks
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Possible flu-like syndrome, mood crash; rebound monoamine deficits.

name: Tyramine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Endogenous trace amine, TAAR1 agonist, indirect sympathomimetic via VMAT2 displacement. Does NOT cross BBB — pharmacologic effects entirely peripheral. The 'cheese reaction': MAOI inhibition allows oral tyramine to escape first-pass MAO → massive peripheral NE release from sympathetic terminals → hypertensive crisis.

routes.notes: Almost entirely degraded by intestinal/hepatic MAO-A; threshold for cheese reaction on MAOI is ~10 mg

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: intestinal MAO-A inhibition + hepatic MAO-A inhibition = absent first-pass degradation
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Hypertensive crisis ('cheese reaction'): 10 mg dietary tyramine causes severe BP spike, 25 mg can be lethal in MAOI users

name: U-47700

binding.notes: Original Upjohn (1978) compound — designed as morphine alternative. ~7.5× more potent than morphine in-vivo despite weaker binding.
Full agonist at MOR; rat antinociception ED50 0.405 mg/kg

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist. Induces ~25% MOR internalisation (similar to DAMGO), in contrast to AH-7921's ~5% (Hsu 2019).

routes.subject_demographics: Male rats, allometric extrapolation to human
routes.notes: Human CL extrapolated 0.944–1.371 L/h/kg via PBPK + IVIVE; no human clinical PK studies exist.

metabolism.notes: Krotulski 2017 — primary metabolite N-desmethyl-U-47700; secondary N,N-didesmethyl. CYP3A4/3A5/2B6/2C19 all contribute.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2C19 PMs likely have reduced clearance; not clinically demonstrated.

notes: Original Upjohn 1978 compound. ~7.5× morphine in-vivo (rat). Was the #1 designer opioid by deaths 2015-2017 before scheduled.

name: U-49900

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Diethylamino homologue of U-47700 (dimethyl → diethyl). MOR agonist per GTPγS in cloned hMOR. Krotulski [35S]GTPγS assay characterised this and seven U-series analogues — U-49900 was a weaker MOR agonist than U-47700.

metabolism.notes: Krotulski 2017 — major metabolite N-desethyl; N,N-didesethyl-N-desmethyl most abundant in urine.

data_gaps_remaining: Specific Ki at MOR/KOR/DOR (only relative GTPγS Emax published)
notes: Direct N-ethyl homologue of U-47700. Less potent functionally; appeared mid-2017 as scheduling workaround.

name: U-51754

binding.notes: Vasudevan 2022 — U-51754 was the most potent KOR agonist in a panel of U-series compounds (EC50 120 nM); shows that pyrrolidine substitution shifts selectivity toward KOR. Unlike U-47700, NOT a μ-selective agonist.
Much weaker than U-47700 at MOR.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: KOR-selective; expect dysphoria/psychotomimesis rather than euphoria; respiratory effects different from MOR opioids.

notes: Often miscategorised as 'methylene-U47700' — actually structurally distinct (pyrrolidine vs dimethylamine) → KOR-selective profile. Naloxone has lower affinity at KOR than MOR; reversal of KOR overdose less predictable.

name: Unifiram

functional.target: excitatory synaptic transmission (rat hippocampus, in vitro)
functional.notes: Same paper group as sunifiram. Reverses NBQX amnesia in mice. As with sunifiram, no direct AMPA receptor binding has been shown — AMPA involvement inferred from antagonism of behavioral effects by AMPA antagonist NBQX.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mechanism uncertain — same caveats as sunifiram. Reported 1000x more potent than piracetam in scopolamine-amnesia reversal, but this potency advantage relies on a single research-group's behavioral series.

data_gaps_remaining: Direct receptor binding at any target
Independent confirmation of preclinical efficacy outside the original group
notes: Same caveats as sunifiram (the two were characterized together by the Romanelli/Galeotti group). Despite frequent vendor classification as 'AMPA PAM,' there is no direct binding evidence. The compound's name and reputation drastically outrun its evidence base.

name: Valerylfentanyl

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full MOR agonist via Gαi/o. β-arrestin bias not reliably established for most fentalogs — fentanyl class is broadly unbiased per Ramos-González 2023.

metabolism.notes: Class-default CYP3A4 N-dealkylation pathway shared with fentanyl. Also 4-ANPP (4-anilino-N-phenethylpiperidine) from amide hydrolysis is a marker of synthesis.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Increased AUC, overdose risk.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Inferred from fentanyl-class — no analogue-specific human data.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Classical opioid; typically shorter than morphine due to higher lipophilicity.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Wooden chest syndrome — class-shared; rapid IV / smoked / IV illicit exposure.

name: Varenicline

binding.notes: Coe et al. 2005 — sub-nM affinity; 45% of nicotine's max efficacy at α4β2.
Highly potent at α6β2; relevant for VTA dopamine modulation.

functional.notes: Partial agonism explains both attenuation of nicotine reward (blocks the full nicotine signal) and reduction of withdrawal craving (maintains baseline dopamine).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Partial agonism at the α4β2 nAChR underlies both efficacy and side-effect profile. By occupying the receptor with sub-maximal activation, varenicline blocks the rewarding effect of inhaled nicotine while preventing acute withdrawal. The 5-HT3 partial agonism contributes to nausea (most common AE).

routes.notes: Oral F >90%, t½ ~24 h, low protein binding, predominantly renal excretion (92% unchanged in urine — minimal metabolism).

metabolism.notes: 92% of dose excreted unchanged in urine — varenicline is essentially a renally-cleared drug.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Modest increase in varenicline AUC

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Minimal — predominantly renal excretion makes pharmacogenetic variability low.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild — possible mood disturbance / vivid dreams during taper

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Nausea (~30% of patients) — most common AE.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Dose-reduce in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30); no hepatic adjustment needed.

notes: FDA-approved smoking cessation aid. Historic neuropsychiatric AE black-box was removed after the EAGLES trial (NCT01456936) found no increased risk vs placebo. The cardiovascular AE signal in patients with CV disease is real but small.

name: Vinpocetine

functional.notes: IC50 in the low μM range; in vivo plasma Cmax (~60-180 nM) is 100-1000× below in-vitro active concentration — a real discrepancy.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Multi-target — PDE1 inhibition raises cAMP/cGMP (cerebral vasodilation); Na+ channel block (anticonvulsant / neuroprotective); IKK inhibition (anti-inflammatory). Plasma concentrations achievable from oral dosing fall well below the IC50s for all three targets, raising mechanistic questions about clinical efficacy.

routes.notes: Very low oral F (~7%) due to first-pass; t½ ~2 h. Major metabolite apovincaminic acid (AVA) has much longer t½ but no defined pharmacology.

data_gaps_remaining: mechanism reconciling in-vivo concentrations with in-vitro IC50s
notes: Apovincamine ester, semisynthetic Vinca minor alkaloid. Used clinically in Eastern Europe and Hungary for stroke/cognitive decline. FDA classified as unsafe in pregnancy (2019 warning) due to risk of miscarriage. Cochrane review: insufficient evidence for cognitive benefit.

name: Zolpidem

binding.notes: Langer & Faure-Halley 1992; Pritchett & Seeburg 1990–1991.
Hanson 2008. Zolpidem effectively does not bind α5-containing GABA-A — defining feature distinguishing it from eszopiclone.

receptor_oligomerisation.functional_consequence: Novel α1/α1 interface modulation discovered for zolpidem at low-γ stoichiometries; may contribute to abuse liability.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: α1-preferring imidazopyridine PAM. The α1G201 residue is the structural basis for selectivity (Pritchett & Seeburg 1991). Sedative-hypnotic action attributed almost exclusively to α1-containing receptors (KO-mouse studies; McKernan 2000).

neuroimaging.finding: [11C]flumazenil displacement at therapeutic doses shows ~25–30% global receptor occupancy at 10 mg.

routes.notes: Short t1/2 ~1.4–4.5 h; rapid onset (Tmax 1.6 h). Substantial first-pass.

metabolism.notes: All metabolites inactive at benzodiazepine site; carboxylic acid metabolites excreted renally.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: AUC doubled, Cmax +30%
AUC reduced ~73%; reduced hypnotic effect

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Minor effect; CYP3A4/5 polymorphism alters CL but redundant pathways limit clinical impact.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Hypnotic tolerance modest at therapeutic doses for ≤4 weeks. Higher doses → tolerance and dependence resembling classical benzos.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Onset within hours of last dose (short t1/2); rebound insomnia, anxiety, autonomic hyperactivity. Seizures and delirium reported at supratherapeutic dependence.

demographic_differences.sex: Females have ~45% higher AUC than males at the same dose (FDA reduced female recommended dose to 5 mg in 2013).
demographic_differences.age: Elderly: Cmax +50%, half-life prolonged; max recommended dose 5 mg.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment: CL reduced ~50%, t1/2 doubled.

notes: Prototype α1-selective Z-drug. Defining feature: no α5 affinity. Complex sleep-related behaviors (sleep-driving, sleep-eating) are FDA-recognized risk; female PK differences led to dose halving.
